incidentSummary.title: Production API Gateway timeout errors
incidentSummary.description: Elevated 502/504 errors on API Gateway affecting customer account endpoints. Error rate spiked to 18% within 30 minutes of deployment v2.4.1.
incidentSummary.businessImpact: Customer account summary and transaction APIs degraded. Estimated 12,400 users affected.

rootCause.summary: Deployment v2.4.1 reduced HikariCP connection pool maximum from 500 to 200, causing upstream connection exhaustion under peak load.
rootCause.detail: The regression was introduced in configuration commit a3f9c21. Under sustained traffic, core-banking-svc exhausted its connection pool, causing API Gateway upstream timeouts and cascading 502/504 responses.
contributingFactors: Connection pool size reduced by 60% without load testing validation
Canary promotion completed before pool metrics stabilized
Circuit breaker thresholds not tuned for reduced pool capacity
No automatic rollback trigger on sustained upstream latency

suggestedFixes.title: Rollback to v2.4.0
suggestedFixes.description: Revert Core Banking API deployment to last known stable version in the primary region.

suggestedFixes.title: Increase connection pool size
suggestedFixes.description: Update HikariCP maxPoolSize from 200 to 400 as an interim stabilization measure.

suggestedFixes.title: Enable regional failover
suggestedFixes.description: Route 100% traffic to the secondary region running v2.4.0 until primary stabilizes.

riskLevel.description: Continued degradation risks SLA breach and customer-facing outage across account services.
